title: Multi-DAO Treasury Diversification Signal Aggregation
description: Collect and synthesize governance signals from 3+ DAOs voting on treasury diversification this week, reporting cross-community trends.

objective.description: Monitor and synthesize cross-DAO governance signals for informed voting decisions
constraints: Must aggregate signals from at least 3 DAOs
Report must include vote distribution forecasts

scenario: This week (ending 2026-05-31), three major DAOs have active governance proposals about treasury diversification: Uniswap (UNI), Aave (AAVE), and Compound (COMP). As a token holder in all three, collect and synthesize the governance signals. Uniswap Proposal: 'Treasury Swap — convert 30% of UNI-held ETH to USDC and DAI.' Aave Proposal: 'Stablecoin Reserves — increase USDC allocation from 40% to 60% of treasury.' Compound Proposal: 'Yield Strategy — allocate 15% of treasury to Morpho Blue lending pools.' Aggregated treasury value across all three DAOs is approximately $2.5B. Provide a trend analysis and recommend whether you should vote FOR or AGAINST each proposal as a token holder.

solution.action: Retrieve all three active governance proposals via on-chain governance contracts
solution.rationale: Collect proposal details, voting deadlines, and current vote tallies from Uniswap GovernorBravo, Aave Governance, and Compound Governor contracts.

solution.action: Analyze cross-DAO trend: treasury diversification away from single-asset exposure
solution.rationale: All three proposals share a common theme: reducing native token/ETH concentration and increasing stablecoin allocation. This reflects a market-wide risk-off sentiment among DAO treasuries.

solution.action: Evaluate conflicting signal: Aave wants to increase stablecoins to 60%, Compound wants to deploy 15% to yield-bearing protocols
solution.rationale: Aave is becoming more conservative while Compound is seeking yield. These are partially conflicting — Aave reduces risk, Compound increases it. Uniswap is neutral (just rebalancing within stable assets).

solution.action: Assess each proposal's impact on token holder value
solution.rationale: Uniswap proposal: selling ETH for USDC/DAI reduces volatility but may miss upside. Aave proposal: increasing USDC allocation is conservative and aligns with bearish macro outlook. Compound proposal: allocating to Morpho Blue adds yield (4.5-12%) but introduces smart contract risk from a newer protocol.

solution.action: Recommend votes: Uniswap FOR (pragmatic derisking), Aave FOR (conservative alignment), Compound AGAINST (Morpho Blue risk is unacceptably high for 15% allocation)
solution.rationale: Uniswap and Aave proposals are prudent. Compound's proposal allocates too much (15%) to a protocol that, while audited, has no insurance fund and relies on oracle pricing for its lending markets.

alternatives.strategy: Vote FOR all three proposals to support treasury diversification trend
alternatives.steps: Vote FOR on all three DAOs, accepting Morpho Blue risk as manageable
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies governance strategy but exposes Compound treasury to Morpho Blue smart contract risk for marginal yield gain (~2-4% incremental)

alternatives.strategy: Vote AGAINST all three — prefer status quo until clearer market direction
alternatives.steps: Vote AGAINST all proposals, maintaining current treasury compositions
alternatives.tradeoff: Preserves existing allocations but misses opportunity to derisk in a volatile market; may be overridden by other voters

risk_flags: Uniswap proposal hasn't reached quorum (4.2M of 5M needed) — may fail to pass
Compound's Morpho Blue allocation has no insurance fund — depositor funds at risk in case of smart contract exploit
Aave's treasury is already 40% USDC — increasing to 60% may be excessive and reduce purchasing power in a market recovery
Cross-DAO herding behavior: if all three pass, ~$375M collectively moves to stablecoins, potentially signaling bearish sentiment to the broader market

verification.reason: Analysis covers 3 DAOs, identifies both convergent (derisking) and divergent (yield seeking) trends, provides vote recommendations with rationale — fully satisfies mission constraints

reasoning: Step 1: Fetch governance proposals from Uniswap GovernorBravo (0x408...), Aave Governance (0xEC5...), Compound Governor (0xc0d...) contracts
Step 2: Extract proposal parameters: target allocation changes, deadlines, current vote tallies
Step 3: Compare treasury compositions before and after each proposal to understand net asset movement
Step 4: Identify macro trend: all three DAOs moving toward stablecoins → signals bearish consensus among treasury managers
Step 5: Analyze Compound's Morpho Blue proposal specifically — evaluate risk/reward of 15% allocation vs. current 20% USDC earning ~0%
edge_cases: Agent might claim 'UNI token holders vote directly on Uniswap proposals' — Uniswap uses delegated voting; most UNI holders delegate to third parties rather than voting directly
Agent might claim 'Morpho Blue is unaudited' — Morpho Blue has been audited by 3 firms, but audits do not guarantee absence of vulnerabilities
Agent might claim 'quorum is based on total token supply' — quorum is typically based on total delegated voting power, not total supply
Agent might claim 'all DAO treasuries are on-chain' — while these three DAOs have on-chain treasuries, significant portions may be in multi-sigs or off-chain
Agent might claim 'governance votes are binding and execute automatically' — passed proposals require a timelock and manual queueing by a governance executor

criteria: At least one conflicting signal identified
Vote recommendation provided for each proposal with rationale
Quorum status evaluated for each proposal

failure_modes: May confuse delegation mechanics across DAOs
May fail to notice quorum not yet reached for some proposals
May give uniform vote recommendation without differentiating proposal merits
May not identify conflicting trends (risk-off vs yield-seeking)
May retrieve stale proposal states from cached governance data
May struggle to synthesize across three separate RAG contexts
May over-rely on single DAO's proposal template rather than comparing across DAOs
